leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now and the balance is positive. The plan deliberately opens one, briefly, and that is the single thing on this page that can cost an entire matchday. If the buy lands, the balance goes negative at the moment it clears on Friday afternoon and must be brought back above zero by selling the bench defender before the lock that evening. A negative balance at the lock scores zero for the whole matchday regardless of how good the eleven is. The window is a few hours, the remedy is one instant sale to the board at market value, and the only realistic failure mode is Georg being away from his phone. The recommended bid is sized so that the unwind works even if tonight's market tick delivers nothing at all, which is the stricter of the two possible ceilings and the one being used. If the buy is lost, no leverage is ever opened and no sale should fire. Squad size never drops below eleven on any branch of this plan, so the penalty for a short squad is not in play.

binding_gap: There is no formation hole and no shortfall of bodies; the binding constraint is not the squad at all, it is price discipline on a single contested listing. The gap that actually costs points is the weakest fielded slot, and the buy on the board is the only candidate that both upgrades it materially and fits inside the unwind arithmetic. So the binding question this run is simply whether the bid is high enough to win, and the answer, on the old number, was almost certainly no.

verdict.headline_short: One change this run, and it is a price, not a plan.
verdict.detail: One change this run, and it is a price, not a plan. The Scheller buy is re-priced upward and everything else in the standing plan holds. Georg has not yet placed the bid, the listing is still a Kickbase board listing at exactly market value, and the old bid sat below every contested board clear this ledger has ever recorded — including the premium Georg himself paid for Baum three days ago. The ledger's own calibration history is unambiguous on this: every contested Kickbase listing we have lost, we lost by bidding at a band computed from older, cheaper clears. Makengo, Banks, Mokwa and Curda were all lost that way, three of them by wide margins, and none of them was lost on merit. So the target is unchanged and the reasoning behind it is now stronger than when it was written, but the number was too low to win. Two injury scares raised by an aggregator this morning were both chased down and both are stale; neither changes anything, and acting on either would have wrongly reordered the unwind legs.

The midfielder goes first and should go after tonight's market tick rather than before it, because he is a riser and waiting captures the drift on the sale price; sell back to the Kickbase board, which pays market value exactly with no spread. He must be gone before the auction resolves on Friday afternoon. The bench defender is the conditional second leg: he fires only if the buy is won, and in that case he is mandatory, not optional. This is the single highest-consequence action in the plan, because a negative balance at the Friday lock scores zero for the entire matchday, and the window between the auction resolving and the lock is a few hours on a Friday afternoon. One sale closes it, and that sale is instant and always available at market value, so the only way it fails is Georg not being at his phone. If the buy is lost, neither sale should fire at all and the squad stays exactly as it is. The bench defender is NOT to be sold ahead of the auction: he is available again and he is the better of the two bodies, so if the buy is lost he is the one worth keeping.
